title: Lesson 7: Near 100 Magic - Add and Subtract Close Numbers
learningGoals: Find how far a number is from 100 (deficit or surplus) in one look.
Add two numbers near 100 by working with their deviations.
Subtract from 100 and 1000 without any borrowing.
coreIdeas: Every number near 100 has a deviation: 97 = 100 - 3, so its deficit is 3.
To add 97 + 98: deviations are -3 and -2. Sum = 200 - 5 = 195.
To subtract: 100 - 37, use All-From-9 Last-From-10. Instant answer.
starterPractice: What is the deviation of 96 from 100? Is it a deficit or surplus?

onboarding.coachIntro: Today you will work with numbers that sit close to 100 and use their small gaps or extra parts to add faster.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at group A. If the learner already knows deviations, jump to group C.

mission.missionPromise: First learn to spot each number's distance from 100, then use that idea to add and subtract with less effort.
mission.successCelebration: Well done. You can now use near-100 thinking to add and subtract these numbers more smoothly.

microLessonPattern: Coach reveals the deviation concept with a number line pointing to 100.
Board shows: 97 is 3 below 100 - draw the gap visually.
Student reads the deviation aloud before computing.
Student finds the deviation of a new number before adding.
Instant feedback highlights the deviation that was wrong.
Review prompt asks the student to add two near-100 numbers by themselves.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 18 XP per exercise group based on difficulty.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Keep the streak counter visible; a correct answer on retry still counts as streak-save.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group earns a themed badge tied to the skill being practised.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Short coach cheer, XP pulse animation, and progress bar moves forward.

reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Re-show the deviation diagram, then give a simpler near-100 pair.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after the student answers the checkpoint correctly.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Missed groups reappear at the start of the next session as warm-up cards.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise A: Spot the distance from 100
sessionFlow.coachHook: Imagine 100 as home base. A number like 97 is only 3 steps below it, and 103 is 3 steps above it. That small distance is the secret we use.
sessionFlow.boardDemo: Draw a short number line with 100 in the center. Mark 97 as 3 below 100 and 103 as 3 above 100 so the gap can be seen before it is named.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Home base is 100. What is the distance of 96 from 100?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Now find the distance of 102 from 100.
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: What is the deviation of 95 from 100?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Yes. You found the distance from 100, which is the key move in this lesson.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: 95 sits 5 below 100, so its deviation is -5. Think of the gap first, not the full subtraction.

sessionFlow.coachHook: To add two near-100 numbers, start from 200 and adjust by both deviations. 97 + 98 = 200 - 3 - 2 = 195. That is it!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect! You added the deviations and hit the right answer instantly.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Subtraction from 100 is even easier! Use All-From-9 Last-From-10. Each digit from 9 except the last digit which comes from 10.

screenplay.teacherLine: Every number near 100 has a secret gap - its deviation! 97 is 3 below 100, so its deviation is -3. 103 is 3 above, so +3. We will use these gaps to add and subtract in a flash!
screenplay.boardAction: Write on board: 97 -> deviation -3. 103 -> deviation +3. Draw a number line around 100.
screenplay.fallbackHint: Deviation = how far the number is from 100. Below 100 is negative, above is positive.

screenplay.teacherLine: To add 97 + 98: instead of adding directly, find both deviations from 100. They are -3 and -2. Start from 200 and apply both: 200 - 3 - 2 = 195. Done in one mental step!
screenplay.checkpointPrompt: What is the deviation of 96 from 100?

screenplay.teacherLine: Watch this! 98 + 97. Deviations: -2 and -3. Base sum: 200. Total deviation: -5. Answer: 195. No long addition needed!
screenplay.boardAction: Show 98 + 97 on board. Highlight deviations: -2 (for 98) and -3 (for 97). Show: 200 - 5 = 195. Box 195.
screenplay.checkpointPrompt: Notice how both steps use only small numbers.
screenplay.fallbackHint: Deviations are the gaps from 100. Sum of gaps is -5. Subtract from 200.

screenplay.teacherLine: Your turn! Try: 99 + 96. What are their deviations from 100? Find both, add them up, and subtract from 200.
screenplay.boardAction: Show 99 + 96. Box two blank spaces: deviation of 99 = ___, deviation of 96 = ___. Final: 200 + ___ = ___.

screenplay.teacherLine: Adding near-100 numbers is always fast. Start from 200, find the two deviations, add them up, and apply to 200. Works whether both are below, both above, or one of each!
screenplay.boardAction: Show three cases: both deficit, both surplus, one each. Animate the sum for each.

screenplay.teacherLine: Near-100 Vedic math works perfectly in real life! Prices, scores, distances - any two numbers near 100 can be added in one mental flash.
screenplay.boardAction: Show: Riya 97 + 98 Science. Animate: 200 - 3 - 2 = 195. Box total score.
screenplay.checkpointPrompt: A book costs 96 rupees and a pen costs 97 rupees. Total cost?
